title: Majburiyat, ruxsat va maslahat: modal fe’llar
goal_uz: Dars oxirida must, have to, mustn't, don't have to, should, can, may va be allowed to ni to‘g‘ri tanlab, qoidalar, taqiqlar, ruxsat va maslahat haqida gapira olasiz.

scenes.title: Modal fe’llar: majburiyat, ruxsat, maslahat
board: must · have to · should · may · can
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda gipotetik shart gaplarni o‘rgandik: “If I were you, I’d...” Bugun modal fe’llar bilan majburiyat, ruxsat va maslahatni ifodalaymiz. O‘zbekchada “kerak” va “mumkin” so‘zlari ko‘p narsani qoplaydi, inglizchada esa ma’no nozikligi ko‘p. Dars oxirida “must”, “have to”, “should”, “may” va “can” ni to‘g‘ri tanlab, qoida va ruxsat haqida aniq gapira olasiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back! Last time we imagined unreal situations. Today we use modal verbs for obligation, permission and advice. By the end, you will choose the right modal and talk about rules clearly.
scenes.say_uz: Yana xush kelibsiz! O‘tgan safar xayoliy vaziyatlarni tasavvur qildik. Bugun majburiyat, ruxsat va maslahat uchun modal fe’llardan foydalanamiz. Dars oxirida kerakli modalni tanlab, qoidalar haqida aniq gapirasiz.

scenes.title: Modal fe’llarning umumiy qoidasi
scenes.say_native: Avval umumiy qoidani eslaylik. Modal fe’llardan keyin fe’lning asosiy shakli keladi, “to” siz. Modal fe’llarga “s” qo‘shilmaydi: “she must”, “he can”, emas “she musts”. Savolda modal gap boshiga chiqadi, inkorda “not” qo‘shiladi: “mustn’t”, “can’t”. O‘zbekchada bu ma’nolar fe’l oxiridagi qo‘shimcha bilan ifodalanadi: “borishi kerak”, “bora oladi”. Inglizchada esa ma’no alohida so‘zda turadi.
scenes.say: Modal verbs are followed by the base form, without to. She must leave now. Can you help me? He should rest. No s for he, she or it.
scenes.say_uz: Modal fe’llardan keyin fe’lning asosiy shakli keladi, to siz. U hozir ketishi kerak. Menga yordam bera olasizmi? U dam olishi kerak. U uchun s qo‘shilmaydi.

scenes.title: Must va have to: majburiyat
board: I must call her. / I have to wear a uniform.

examples.t: I must call my mother tonight.
Students have to wear a uniform.

scenes.say_native: Majburiyat uchun ikkita asosiy fe’l bor. “Must” odatda gapiruvchining o‘z fikri, shaxsiy zaruratini bildiradi: “I must call my mother” — men shunday deb hisoblayman. “Have to” esa tashqaridan kelgan majburiyat, ya’ni qoida, qonun, ish tartibi: “Students have to wear a uniform”. Amalda farq ba’zan kichik, ayniqsa Britaniya ingliz tilida. Lekin “have to” kundalik nutqda ko‘proq uchraydi, “must” esa rasmiy yozuv va ko‘rsatmalarda.
scenes.say: I must call my mother tonight. That is my own feeling. Students have to wear a uniform. That is the school's rule. In everyday speech, have to is very common.
scenes.say_uz: Bugun onamga qo‘ng‘iroq qilishim kerak. Bu mening shaxsiy hissiyotim. O‘quvchilar forma kiyishi shart. Bu maktab qoidasi. Kundalik nutqda have to juda keng tarqalgan.

scenes.title: Have to: shakllari
board: Do I have to...? / She doesn't have to...
Past: had to · Future: will have to

examples.t: She has to get up at six.
Do we have to bring a laptop?

scenes.say_native: “Have to” oddiy fe’lga o‘xshab ishlaydi. Hozirgi zamonda “he, she, it” bilan “has to”. Savol va inkor “do” yoki “does” bilan tuziladi: “Do I have to?”, “She doesn’t have to”. Muhim nuqta: “must” ning o‘tmish va kelasi shakli yo‘q. O‘tmishda “had to”, kelajakda “will have to” deymiz: “I had to wait for an hour.” Shuning uchun “have to” siz uchun modal fe’lning universal o‘rinbosari.
scenes.say: She has to get up at six. Do we have to bring a laptop? I had to wait for an hour yesterday. Next year, you will have to pay more.
scenes.say_uz: U oltida turishi kerak. Noutbuk olib kelishimiz shartmi? Kecha bir soat kutishimga to‘g‘ri keldi. Kelasi yil ko‘proq to‘lashingizga to‘g‘ri keladi.

scenes.title: Must o‘tmishda yo‘q
board: ✗ She musts go. ✓ She must go.
scenes.say_native: Tipik xato: o‘tmish haqida gapirganda “must” ni ishlatish. “Must” ning o‘tmish shakli yo‘q, shuning uchun “kecha kutishim kerak edi” inglizchada “I had to wait yesterday” bo‘ladi. Ikkinchi xato: “she musts” deyish. Modal fe’lga hech qachon “s” qo‘shilmaydi. Uchinchi xato: “must to go” kabi “to” qo‘yish. O‘zbekchada fe’l har bir zamonda o‘z qo‘shimchasini oladi, inglizchada esa “must” qotib qolgan shakl, shuning uchun o‘tmishda boshqa fe’l kerak.
scenes.say: Say: I had to wait yesterday. Not: I must wait yesterday. And remember: she must go, not she musts go, and not must to go.
scenes.say_uz: Ayting: kecha kutishimga to‘g‘ri keldi. “I must wait yesterday” demang. Va eslang: she must go, she musts go emas, must to go ham emas.

scenes.title: Must yoki have to?
board: 1) Yesterday I (must / had to) stay late.
2) Visitors (must / have to) sign in. It's the rule.
3) She (has to / musts) work on Saturday.
scenes.say_native: Uchta gapda to‘g‘ri shaklni tanlang. Birinchisida kecha haqida gap ketyapti, o‘tmishga e’tibor bering. Ikkinchisida bino qoidasi haqida gap bor. Uchinchisida uchinchi shaxs bor, “s” ning o‘rniga to‘g‘ri shaklni tanlang. To‘liq gapni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Choose the correct form. Yesterday I must or had to stay late. Visitors must or have to sign in. She has to or musts work on Saturday.
scenes.say_uz: To‘g‘ri shaklni tanlang. Kecha kech qolishimga to‘g‘ri keldi. Mehmonlar ro‘yxatdan o‘tishi shart. U shanba kuni ishlashi kerak.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “Yesterday I had to stay late”, chunki o‘tmish. Ikkinchi: “Visitors must sign in” yoki “have to sign in”; ikkalasi ham to‘g‘ri, chunki bu rasmiy qoida. Uchinchi: “She has to work on Saturday”. “Musts” degan shakl umuman yo‘q. Agar hamma javoblaringiz to‘g‘ri bo‘lsa, majburiyat qismini yaxshi o‘zlashtirdingiz.
scenes.say: Yesterday I had to stay late. Visitors must sign in, or have to sign in. She has to work on Saturday.
scenes.say_uz: Kecha kech qolishimga to‘g‘ri keldi. Mehmonlar ro‘yxatdan o‘tishi shart. U shanba kuni ishlashi kerak.

scenes.title: Mustn’t va don’t have to

examples.t: You don't have to come. It's optional.

scenes.say_native: Bu darsning eng muhim farqi. “Mustn’t” taqiqni bildiradi: “You mustn’t smoke here” — chekish mumkin emas. “Don’t have to” esa majburiyat yo‘qligini bildiradi: “You don’t have to come” — kelsangiz ham bo‘ladi, kelmasangiz ham. Britaniya ingliz tilida “needn’t” ham ishlatiladi: “You needn’t come”. O‘zbekchada ikkalasi ham “kerak emas” bo‘lib eshitilishi mumkin, shuning uchun ularni aralashtirib yuborish oson, lekin ma’no butunlay boshqa.
scenes.say: You mustn't smoke here. It is forbidden. You don't have to come. It is optional. British speakers also say: you needn't come.
scenes.say_uz: Bu yerda chekish mumkin emas. Bu taqiqlangan. Kelishingiz shart emas. Bu ixtiyoriy. Britaniyaliklar you needn't come ham deydi.

scenes.title: Taqiq va shart emas
board: ✗ You don't have to drive fast here. (taqiq)
✓ You don't have to drive. I can take you.
scenes.say_native: Mana tipik xato: “You don’t have to drive fast here”. Siz taqiqlamoqchisiz, lekin gap “tez haydashingiz shart emas” degan ma’noni beradi, ya’ni tez haydash mumkin, faqat zarur emas. To‘g‘risi: “You mustn’t drive fast here”. Aksincha, “You mustn’t come” deyish — kelish taqiqlangan degani, siz esa shunchaki ixtiyoriylikni aytmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, “You don’t have to come” deng. Doim o‘zingizdan so‘rang: bu taqiqmi yoki shunchaki ixtiyoriymi?
scenes.say: You mustn't drive fast here. That is forbidden. You don't have to drive today. I can take you. Forbidden or optional? Choose carefully.
scenes.say_uz: Bu yerda tez haydash mumkin emas. Bu taqiqlangan. Bugun haydashingiz shart emas. Sizni men olib boraman. Taqiqmi yoki ixtiyoriymi? Ehtiyot bo‘lib tanlang.

scenes.title: Taqiqmi yoki shart emasmi?
board: 2) It's Sunday. You ___ get up early.
3) Fire exit! You ___ block this door.
scenes.say_native: Uchta vaziyat. Har birida “mustn’t” yoki “don’t have to” ni tanlang. Birinchi: kutubxonada baland ovozda gapirish. Ikkinchi: yakshanba, erta turish kerakmi? Uchinchi: yong‘in chiqish eshigini to‘sib qo‘yish. Avval taqiqmi yoki ixtiyoriylikmi, deb o‘ylang, keyin javob bering.
scenes.say: Choose mustn't or don't have to. In the library, you talk loudly. On Sunday, you get up early. At the fire exit, you block this door.
scenes.say_uz: Mustn't yoki don't have to ni tanlang. Kutubxonada baland ovozda gapirish. Yakshanba kuni erta turish. Yong‘in chiqish eshigini to‘sish.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “You mustn’t talk loudly”, chunki bu taqiq. Ikkinchi: “You don’t have to get up early”, yakshanba kuni majburiyat yo‘q, istasangiz erta turasiz. Uchinchi: “You mustn’t block this door”, bu xavfsizlik uchun taqiq. Shuni eslab qoling: “mustn’t” — qilmang, “don’t have to” — qilsangiz ham, qilmasangiz ham bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: You mustn't talk loudly. You don't have to get up early. You mustn't block this door.
scenes.say_uz: Baland ovozda gapirmang. Erta turishingiz shart emas. Bu eshikni to‘smang.

scenes.title: Should va ought to: maslahat

examples.t: You'd better hurry, or you'll miss the train.

scenes.say_native: Maslahat uchun “should” ishlatiladi: “You should drink more water.” U “must” dan yumshoqroq: bu majburiyat emas, yaxshi fikr. “Ought to” ma’no jihatdan deyarli bir xil, biroq biroz rasmiyroq. “Had better” esa kuchliroq: agar maslahatga amal qilmasangiz, yomon oqibat bo‘ladi. Shakli o‘tmishdagidek ko‘rinsa ham, ma’no hozirgi yoki kelasi zamon. Inkor: “You shouldn’t”, “You’d better not”. O‘zbekchada “-ishingiz kerak” va “-ganingiz ma’qul” iboralariga mos.
scenes.say: You should drink more water. You ought to see a doctor. You'd better hurry, or you'll miss the train. You shouldn't stay up so late.
scenes.say_uz: Ko‘proq suv ichishingiz kerak. Shifokorga borishingiz kerak. Shoshilganingiz ma’qul, bo‘lmasa poyezddan qolasiz. Bunchalik kech yotmasligingiz kerak.

scenes.title: Should bilan xatolar
board: ✗ You should to see a doctor.
✗ You'd better to go. ✓ You'd better go.
scenes.say_native: Maslahatda ikki xato uchraydi. Birinchi: “should” dan keyin “to” qo‘yish. “You should to see” noto‘g‘ri, to‘g‘risi “You should see”. Xuddi shu qoida “had better” ga ham tegishli: “You’d better go”, “to” siz. Ikkinchi nuqta: “ought to” da “to” bor, uni tushirib qoldirmang, “ought go” noto‘g‘ri. Uchinchi: “had better” da “had” o‘tmish ma’noda emas, shuning uchun “You’d better yesterday” demang.
scenes.say: Say: you should see a doctor. You'd better go now. But: you ought to see a doctor, with to. Not: you should to see.
scenes.say_uz: Ayting: shifokorga borishingiz kerak. Hozir ketganingiz ma’qul. Lekin ought to da to bor. “You should to see” demang.

scenes.title: Maslahat bering
board: 1) I have a cold. → You should ...
2) My train leaves in five minutes! → You'd better ...
3) I eat fast food every day. → You shouldn't ...
scenes.say_native: Uchta vaziyatga mos maslahat bering. Birinchi: sizda shamollash bor, do‘stingiz nima qilishi kerak? Ikkinchi: poyezd besh daqiqadan keyin jo‘naydi, kuchli ogohlantirish uchun “had better” ishlating. Uchinchi: odam har kuni tez ovqat yeydi, inkor maslahat bering. Baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Give advice. I have a cold. My train leaves in five minutes! I eat fast food every day.
scenes.say_uz: Maslahat bering. Men shamollaganman. Poyezdim besh daqiqadan keyin jo‘naydi! Men har kuni tez ovqat yeyman.

scenes.title: Namuna javoblar
board: 1) You should stay in bed and rest.
3) You shouldn't eat it every day.
scenes.say_native: Namunalar. Birinchi: “You should stay in bed and drink hot tea.” Ikkinchi: “You’d better run!”, vaziyat shoshilinch, shuning uchun kuchli shakl. Uchinchi: “You shouldn’t eat it every day”. Sizniki farq qilishi mumkin, masalan “You ought to see a doctor”. Asosiysi, modaldan keyin “to” siz fe’l kelsin. Faqat “ought to” bundan mustasno.
scenes.say: You should stay in bed and drink hot tea. You'd better run! You shouldn't eat it every day.
scenes.say_uz: Yotib dam oling va issiq choy iching. Yuguring! Buni har kuni yemasligingiz kerak.

scenes.title: Ruxsat: can, may, could

examples.t: May I use your phone, please?

scenes.say_native: Ruxsat so‘rashning uch darajasi bor. “Can I...?” — oddiy, do‘stlar va oila orasida. “Could I...?” — muloyimroq, notanish yoki katta kishiga. “May I...?” — eng rasmiy, ishxonada, mehmonxonada, imtihonda. Ruxsat berish uchun “Yes, of course” yoki “Sure” deyiladi. “You may” rasmiy ruxsat, “you can” esa oddiy. O‘zbekchada “mumkinmi?” bitta so‘z, inglizchada esa vaziyatga qarab shakl tanlanadi.
scenes.say: Can I sit here? Could I borrow your pen? May I use your phone, please? Yes, of course. Sure, go ahead.
scenes.say_uz: Bu yerga o‘tirsam bo‘ladimi? Ruchkangizni olsam bo‘ladimi? Telefoningizdan foydalansam maylimi? Albatta. Marhamat.

scenes.title: Be allowed to
board: You're not allowed to park here.

examples.t: Children are not allowed to enter.
We weren't allowed to use phones in class.
examples.uz: Darsda telefon ishlatishga ruxsat yo‘q edi.

scenes.say_native: Qoida va ruxsatni ifodalashning yana bir yo‘li — “be allowed to”. U “can” ga yaqin, lekin qoida yoki qonun nuqtai nazaridan: “You’re not allowed to park here”. Eng qulay jihati, u o‘tmishda ham ishlaydi: “We weren’t allowed to use phones.” Chunki “may” ning o‘tmishi ruxsat uchun yo‘q. “Can” ning o‘tmishi “could” ruxsat uchun faqat umumiy odatda ishlatiladi, bitta aniq holat uchun “was allowed to” aytamiz. Bu o‘zbekchadagi “ruxsat etilgan” ga o‘xshaydi.
scenes.say: You're not allowed to park here. Children are not allowed to enter. We weren't allowed to use phones in class when I was at school.
scenes.say_uz: Bu yerga to‘xtash mumkin emas. Bolalarga kirish mumkin emas. Men maktabda o‘qiganimda darsda telefon ishlatishga ruxsat yo‘q edi.

scenes.title: Ruxsatdagi xatolar
board: ✗ Give me your pen! (qo‘pol) ✓ Could I borrow your pen?
scenes.say_native: Ruxsat so‘rashda ikkita xato bor. Birinchisi grammatik: “Can I to go?” — modaldan keyin “to” qo‘yish. To‘g‘risi “Can I go?”. Ikkinchisi — muloyimlik. Notanish odamga “Give me your pen” deyish buyruq kabi eshitiladi. “Could I borrow your pen?” yoki “Would you mind...?” ancha yaxshi. O‘zbekchada “bering” deyish odatiy, inglizchada esa iltimosni savol shaklida berish muloyimlik belgisi. Shuni unutmang.
scenes.say: Say: could I borrow your pen? Not: give me your pen. And say can I go, not can I to go.
scenes.say_uz: Ayting: ruchkangizni olsam bo‘ladimi? “Give me your pen” demang. Va can I go deng, can I to go emas.

scenes.title: Muloyim iltimos
board: 1) Ask your friend for a lift (informal).
2) Ask a stranger to sit down (polite).
3) Ask your boss for a day off (formal).
scenes.say_native: Uchta vaziyat. Birinchi: do‘stingizdan mashinada olib ketishni so‘rang, oddiy shakl. Ikkinchi: notanish odamdan uning yonida o‘tirishga ruxsat so‘rang, muloyim shakl. Uchinchi: rahbaringizdan bir kunlik ta’til so‘rang, eng rasmiy shakl. Har biriga mos modalni tanlang.
scenes.say: Ask for permission. Ask your friend for a lift. Ask a stranger if you can sit down. Ask your boss for a day off.
scenes.say_uz: Ruxsat so‘rang. Do‘stingizdan mashinada olib ketishni so‘rang. Notanishdan o‘tirsam bo‘ladimi, deb so‘rang. Rahbaringizdan bir kunlik ta’til so‘rang.

scenes.title: Namuna javoblar
board: 3) May I take a day off tomorrow?
scenes.say_native: Namunalar. Birinchi: “Can I get a lift with you?” Ikkinchi: “Excuse me, could I sit here?” Uchinchi: “Excuse me, may I take a day off tomorrow?” Ko‘rdingizmi, darajalar o‘zgaryapti: oddiydan rasmiygacha. “Excuse me” va “please” qo‘shsangiz, yanada yoqimli chiqadi. Rahbar bilan gaplashganda “Would it be possible...?” ham ishlaydi, lekin buni keyinroq o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Can I get a lift with you? Excuse me, could I sit here? Excuse me, may I take a day off tomorrow?
scenes.say_uz: Siz bilan birga ketsam bo‘ladimi? Kechirasiz, bu yerga o‘tirsam bo‘ladimi? Kechirasiz, ertaga bir kun dam olsam maylimi?

scenes.title: Modal ma’nolari kontekstda

examples.t: He must be tired. He's worked all day.
examples.uz: U charchagan bo‘lsa kerak. U kun bo‘yi ishladi.

scenes.say_native: Modal fe’llar bir nechta ma’noga ega. “Must” majburiyat bildiradi, lekin yana ishonchli taxmin ham: “He must be tired” — u, albatta, charchagan, chunki kun bo‘yi ishlagan. “May” ruxsat ham, ehtimol ham: “It may rain later” — yomg‘ir yog‘ishi mumkin. “Can” ning uchta ma’nosi bor: qobiliyat — “I can swim”, ruxsat — “Can I go?”, imkoniyat — “It can be cold here”. Ma’noni kontekstdan bilib olasiz. Bu yerda taxmin haqida faqat tanishib chiqamiz.
scenes.say: He must be tired. He's worked all day. It may rain later. She can swim, and she can speak three languages.
scenes.say_uz: U charchagan bo‘lsa kerak. U kun bo‘yi ishladi. Keyinroq yomg‘ir yog‘ishi mumkin. U suzishni biladi va uch tilda gapira oladi.

scenes.title: Qaysi ma’no?
board: 1) You must wear a seat belt.
2) You must be hungry after that run!
scenes.say_native: Uchta gapning modal ma’nosini aniqlang. Birinchi gap: majburiyatmi yoki taxminmi? Ikkinchi: yugurgandan keyin odam nimani his qiladi, taxmin yoki majburiyatmi? Uchinchi: qobiliyatmi yoki ruxsatmi? Javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting. Ikkinchi gapda “must” bu yerda majburiyat emasligini sezing: gapiruvchi dalilga qarab xulosa chiqaryapti.
scenes.say: What does each modal mean? You must wear a seat belt. You must be hungry after that run! Can you swim?
scenes.say_uz: Har bir modalning ma’nosi nima? Xavfsizlik kamarini taqishingiz shart. Shu yugurishdan keyin ochqagan bo‘lsangiz kerak! Suzishni bilasizmi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: majburiyat, xavfsizlik qoidasi. Ikkinchi: taxmin, ya’ni “siz ochqagan bo‘lsangiz kerak”, chunki dalil bor — yugurish. Uchinchi: qobiliyat, ya’ni “suzishni bilasizmi?” Bitta modal turli kontekstda turli ma’no beradi, shuning uchun gapning ma’nosiga qaraymiz. Bu ko‘nikma ayniqsa tinglash va o‘qishda juda kerak bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: The first is obligation. The second is certainty, because you ran. The third is ability.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchisi majburiyat. Ikkinchisi taxmin, chunki yugurdingiz. Uchinchisi qobiliyat.

scenes.title: Tinglang: yangi ish kuni
board: Anna: Do I have to wear a suit?
Mark: No, you don't have to, but you should look smart.
Mark: You mustn't use your phone at the desk.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi dialogni tinglang. Anna yangi ishga birinchi kuni keldi va Mark undan qoidalarni so‘rayapti. Dialogda majburiyat, taqiq va maslahat bor. Har bir modalni ushlashga harakat qiling: “have to”, “don’t have to”, “should” va “mustn’t”. Keyin savollarga javob beramiz.
scenes.say: Anna: Do I have to wear a suit? Mark: No, you don't have to, but you should look smart. Anna: Can I bring my own laptop? Mark: Yes, but you mustn't use your phone at the desk. And you have to sign in every morning.
scenes.say_uz: Anna: Kostyum kiyishim shartmi? Mark: Yo‘q, shart emas, lekin chiroyli kiyinishing kerak. Anna: O‘z noutbukimni olib kelsam bo‘ladimi? Mark: Ha, lekin stolda telefondan foydalanish mumkin emas. Har ertalab ro‘yxatdan o‘tishing shart.

scenes.title: Dialog bo‘yicha savollar
board: 1) Does Anna have to wear a suit?
2) Is Anna allowed to bring a laptop?
3) What mustn't she do at the desk? What must she do every morning?
scenes.say_native: Dialogni eslab, savollarga javob bering. Birinchi: Anna kostyum kiyishi shartmi? Ikkinchi: u o‘z noutbukini olib kelishi mumkinmi? Uchinchi: stolda nima qilish mumkin emas va har ertalab nima shart? Javoblar to‘liq gap bo‘lsin va mos modalni ishlating, savollardagi so‘zlarni qaytaring.
scenes.say: Answer the questions. Does Anna have to wear a suit? Is she allowed to bring a laptop? What mustn't she do, and what does she have to do every morning?
scenes.say_uz: Savollarga javob bering. Annaning kostyum kiyishi shartmi? Noutbuk olib kelishi mumkinmi? U nimani qilmasligi va har ertalab nima qilishi kerak?

scenes.title: Dialog javoblari
board: 3) mustn't use her phone / has to sign in
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: yo‘q, Anna kostyum kiyishi shart emas, “she doesn’t have to”, lekin chiroyli kiyinishi tavsiya qilinadi. Ikkinchi: ha, noutbukni olib kelishi mumkin. Uchinchi: stolda telefondan foydalanishi mumkin emas, “she mustn’t use her phone”, va har ertalab ro‘yxatdan o‘tishi shart, “she has to sign in”. Taqiq, shart emas va majburiyat uchta alohida ma’no.
scenes.say: No, she doesn't have to wear a suit. Yes, she can bring her laptop. She mustn't use her phone at the desk, and she has to sign in every morning.
scenes.say_uz: Yo‘q, u kostyum kiyishi shart emas. Ha, u noutbukni olib kelishi mumkin. U stolda telefondan foydalanmasligi kerak va har ertalab ro‘yxatdan o‘tishi shart.

scenes.title: Tinglang: mehmonxona qabuli
board: Guest: May I check in early, please?
Clerk: I'm afraid you can't, but you may leave your bags.
Clerk: Breakfast is until ten. You needn't book.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog mehmonxonada bo‘ladi. Mehmon muloyim va rasmiy ruxsat so‘rayapti, xodim esa rad etadi va muqobil taklif beradi. Rasmiy shakllarni eshiting: “May I...”, “I’m afraid you can’t”, “you may”. Bu qoliplar xizmat sohasida juda ko‘p ishlatiladi.
scenes.say: Guest: May I check in early, please? Clerk: I'm afraid you can't. Rooms are ready at two. But you may leave your bags here. Guest: Thank you. Do I have to book breakfast? Clerk: No, you needn't. It's served until ten.
scenes.say_uz: Mehmon: Barvaqt joylashsam bo‘ladimi? Xodim: Afsuski, bo‘lmaydi. Xonalar soat ikkida tayyor bo‘ladi. Lekin sumkalaringizni shu yerda qoldirishingiz mumkin. Mehmon: Rahmat. Nonushtani buyurtma qilishim shartmi? Xodim: Yo‘q, shart emas. U soat o‘ngacha beriladi.

scenes.title: Savollar: mehmonxona
board: 1) Can the guest check in early?
2) What may he do with his bags?
3) Does he have to book breakfast?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savolga javob bering. Birinchi: mehmon barvaqt joylasha oladimi? Ikkinchi: u sumkalari bilan nima qilishi mumkin? Uchinchi: nonushtani oldindan buyurtma qilishi shartmi? Javoblaringizda mos modal fe’lni ishlating, masalan “can’t”, “may” va “needn’t”.
scenes.say: Answer the questions. Can the guest check in early? What may he do with his bags? Does he have to book breakfast?
scenes.say_uz: Savollarga javob bering. Mehmon barvaqt joylasha oladimi? U sumkalari bilan nima qilishi mumkin? Nonushtani buyurtma qilishi shartmi?

scenes.title: Dialog javoblari
board: 2) He may leave them at reception.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: yo‘q, mehmon barvaqt joylasha olmaydi, xonalar soat ikkida tayyor. Ikkinchi: u sumkalarini qabulxonada qoldirishi mumkin, “he may leave them”. Uchinchi: yo‘q, nonushtani oldindan buyurtma qilishi shart emas, “he needn’t book”, yoki “he doesn’t have to”. Eslab qoling, “I’m afraid you can’t” — rad etishning muloyim usuli.
scenes.say: No, he can't check in early. He may leave his bags at reception. No, he needn't book breakfast.
scenes.say_uz: Yo‘q, barvaqt joylasha olmaydi. U sumkalarini qabulxonada qoldirishi mumkin. Yo‘q, nonushtani buyurtma qilishi shart emas.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: modal fe’llar nutqda
scenes.say_native: Talaffuzda “can” va “can’t” ni ajratish juda muhim. Tasdiq gapda “can” zaif aytiladi, deyarli “kn”, va urg‘u fe’lga tushadi: “I can SWIM”. Inkorda “can’t” kuchli va uzun: Britaniya ingliz tilida “kaant”. “Have to” tez aytilganda “hafta”, “has to” — “hasta”. “Mustn’t” da birinchi “t” deyarli eshitilmaydi: “mussnt”. Amerika ingliz tilida “can’t” qisqaroq, lekin ohang va urg‘u baribir farq qiladi.
scenes.say: I can swim. I can't swim. I have to go. She has to work. You mustn't be late.
scenes.say_uz: Men suzishni bilaman. Men suzishni bilmayman. Ketishim kerak. U ishlashi kerak. Kech qolmasligingiz kerak.

scenes.title: Talaffuzni mashq qiling
board: I can swim, but I can't dive.
scenes.say_native: Uchta gapni takrorlang. Birinchisida “can” ni zaif, “can’t” ni kuchli ayting, farqni his qiling. Ikkinchisida “have to” ni “hafta” kabi bog‘lab ayting. Uchinchisida “mustn’t” dagi tovushlarni aniq ayting. Ikki marta takrorlang, har safar tezroq, lekin tushunarli bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: I can swim, but I can't dive. I have to go now. You mustn't be late.
scenes.say_uz: Men suzishni bilaman, lekin sho‘ng‘ishni bilmayman. Hozir ketishim kerak. Kech qolmasligingiz kerak.

scenes.title: Model talaffuz
scenes.say_native: Yaxshi. Esda tuting: tasdiqda “can” zaif, inkorda “can’t” kuchli va uzun. Aynan shu farq eshitish orqali ma’noni ajratishga yordam beradi. “Have to” da “v” tovushi “f” ga yaqinlashadi, shuning uchun “hafta” eshitiladi, bunga ajablanmang. Shu odatlarni o‘zlashtirsangiz, tezkor nutqni tushunish ancha osonlashadi, o‘zingizning nutqingiz ham tabiiy bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: I can swim, but I can't dive. I have to go now. You mustn't be late.
scenes.say_uz: Men suzishni bilaman, lekin sho‘ng‘ishni bilmayman. Hozir ketishim kerak. Kech qolmasligingiz kerak.

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq: qoidalar
board: 1) Say 2 things you must / have to do at work or school.
3) Say 1 thing you don't have to do.
scenes.say_native: Endi o‘zingiz gapirasiz. Ishxonangiz yoki maktabingiz qoidalari haqida beshta gap ayting. Ikkitasi majburiyat haqida, “must” yoki “have to” bilan. Ikkitasi taqiq haqida, “mustn’t” bilan. Bittasi shart emas haqida, “don’t have to” bilan. Har bir modalni qanday ma’noda ishlatayotganingizni o‘ylab gapiring.
scenes.say: Now you speak. Tell me two things you must or have to do at work or school. Two things you mustn't do. One thing you don't have to do.
scenes.say_uz: Endi siz gapiring. Ishda yoki maktabda qilishingiz shart bo‘lgan ikki narsani ayting. Qilmasligingiz kerak bo‘lgan ikki narsani ayting. Qilishingiz shart bo‘lmagan bitta narsani ayting.

scenes.title: Namuna javob
board: We have to arrive by eight.
We mustn't use phones in class.
We don't have to wear a uniform on Fridays.
scenes.say_native: Namuna. “We have to arrive by eight. We must hand in homework on time. We mustn’t use phones in class. We mustn’t cheat in exams. We don’t have to wear a uniform on Fridays.” Sizning qoidalaringiz albatta boshqacha. Tekshiring: majburiyat uchun “have to” yoki “must”, taqiq uchun “mustn’t”, ixtiyoriy narsa uchun “don’t have to”. Uchalasi aralashib ketmagan bo‘lsa, topshiriq bajarildi.
scenes.say: We have to arrive by eight. We must hand in homework on time. We mustn't use phones in class. We don't have to wear a uniform on Fridays.
scenes.say_uz: Biz soat sakkizgacha kelishimiz kerak. Uy vazifasini o‘z vaqtida topshirishimiz shart. Darsda telefon ishlatmasligimiz kerak. Juma kuni forma kiyishimiz shart emas.

scenes.title: Dars yakuni
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Majburiyat uchun “must” yoki “have to”, o‘tmishda “had to”. Taqiq uchun “mustn’t”, majburiyat yo‘qligi uchun “don’t have to” yoki “needn’t”. Maslahat uchun “should”, “ought to” va “had better”. Ruxsat uchun “can”, “could”, “may”, “be allowed to”. Modaldan keyin “to” siz fe’l keladi. Siz bugun ajoyib ishladingiz, barakalla!
scenes.say: Today you learned obligation, prohibition, advice and permission. Remember: mustn't means forbidden, and don't have to means not necessary. Well done!
scenes.say_uz: Bugun majburiyat, taqiq, maslahat va ruxsatni o‘rgandingiz. Eslang: mustn't taqiq, don't have to esa shart emas. Barakalla!

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
board: Homework: rules of your school or workplace
Use must / mustn't / don't have to / can
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: o‘z maktabingiz yoki ish joyingiz qoidalarini yozing. Kamida sakkizta qoida bo‘lsin: majburiyat, taqiq, shart emas va ruxsat haqida. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: “mustn’t” va “don’t have to” to‘g‘ri ajratilgan, modaldan keyin “to” yo‘q. Keyingi darsda majhul nisbat asoslarini o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Your homework: write the rules of your school or workplace. Use must, mustn't, don't have to and can. See you next time!
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifangiz: maktabingiz yoki ish joyingiz qoidalarini yozing. Must, mustn't, don't have to va can ishlating. Keyingi darsda ko‘rishamiz!

homework_uz: O‘z maktabingiz yoki ish joyingiz qoidalarini yozing: kamida sakkizta gap, ular majburiyat, taqiq, shart emas va ruxsatni o‘z ichiga olsin. Mezon: mustn't va don't have to to‘g‘ri ajratilgan, modaldan keyin to yo‘q, o‘tmish uchun had to ishlatilgan.

quiz.q: Yesterday I ___ wait for an hour.
quiz.why_uz: Must ning o‘tmish shakli yo‘q, had to ishlatiladi.

quiz.q: It's Sunday. You ___ get up early.

quiz.why_uz: Modal fe’lga s qo‘shilmaydi, keyin to siz fe’l keladi.

quiz.q: You ___ see a doctor. You look ill.
Which is the most formal request?
quiz.why_uz: May I — eng rasmiy ruxsat so‘rash shakli.

quiz.q: We ___ use phones in class when I was young.
He's worked all day. He ___ be tired.

quiz.why_uz: Had better kuchli maslahat yoki ogohlantirish.
